Registry/index UI must not smuggle system telemetry (recall p50/p95) — belongs to OS Eval, fix was DELETE not restyle (Connections-panel family) | An honesty badge is only as truthful as the signal it reads: last_synced stamped unconditionally made an empty-graph mount falsely 'indexed' — UI honesty fix REQUIRED the backend total>0 guard | kind judgement by 'contains any parseable file' is over-eager
judge by STRUCTURAL repo marker (.git/manifest), a stray .py is not a repo

When a new writer targets a SHARED store, it MUST be tested against the EXISTING maintenance passes over that store, not just its own read path — my tests never ran a Knowledge/ sync after a docs-mount index, so the CRITICAL silent-wipe (sync prune treats mount: keys as deleted files) was invisible until the adversarial gate. Shared-store contamination is a distinct test axis. | The systematic fix for a 'needs an LLM/chat step' gap was to DELETE the LLM step and reuse the mechanical substrate we already had (chunk_markdown + KnowledgeStore) — the briefing design was over-engineering that manufactured the gap. | A namespaced key (mount:<id>/) in a shared index needs BOTH: collision-avoidance (distinct prefix) AND exclusion from every OTHER owner's prune/normalize logic — half of that (collision) is obvious, the other half (other owners must skip it) is the one that silently breaks.

[pitfall] When HARDENING a guard, the NEW safe-path you add can itself have an unguarded escape edge — both Gate-2 HIGHs this run were this class: the cp -t dest-parse handled the separated form but the BUNDLED short-flag variant (cp -rt/-ft <store>) fell through to the generic flag-drop → fail-open

the isolate EXDEV branch called shutil.move to preserve-across-device but left the copy UNGUARDED so a mid-copy ENOSPC escaped as bare OSError, bypassing the IsolationError contract. Tell: after adding a new branch to a guard (a flag-parse case, a fallback path), enumerate that branch's OWN failure/variant space, not just the happy path — the escape edge hides one level inside the fix.

[pitfall] A pytest.raises((SpecificError, Exception)) matcher is near-vacuous on the type dimension — Exception swallows everything, so the 'must raise AS SpecificError' contract is untested. Use pytest.raises(SpecificError) alone when the propagation TYPE is the contract (meta-review caught this)

[guideline] Adversarial findings are LEADS not verdicts (R2): 5 Gate-2 findings, verified each against source — 2 were real+mine (fixed+mutation-proven), 3 were genuine-but-pre-existing/out-of-scope follow-ups correctly logged not fixed (avoided scope creep XG warned against).
